To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sensitivity of the processes e-e- →e-e- and e+e-→ e+e- to electron-electron (or muon-muon) contact-interactions at a Linear Collider is significantly enhanced when the beams are polarized.

polarized cross section measurement in the process e+e-→e+e- at a Linear collider running in e+e- mode is a powerful tool for model-independent tests of contact interactions in electron-electron scattering, and that the reach in the contact coupling constant is about 10 TeV.

the sensitivity of the e+e- process to the contact interaction is dominated by the polarized differential cross section in the high-energy region, while for the e-e- process the sensitivity is mainly determined by the unpolarized total cross section at the low-energy threshold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of electron-electron interactions in the framework of the Standard Model.
the study of the effects of new physics in the form of contact interactions on electron-electron scattering processes at a future Linear Collider.
the study of new physics in electron-positron collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reach for the contact coupling is about 1/10 of that for the four-fermion contact coupling.

the proposed Linear Collider, with its polarized e+e- beams, would provide the first experimental test of the lepton sector, with a sensitivity to contact couplings that is competitive with the present limits obtained in the quark sector.

the proposed Linear Collider, with polarized beams, will allow a model-independent determination of the contact-interactions parameters at a level of 1-2 orders of magnitude better than the current limits from LEP and SLC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 1 TeV polarized Linear Collider would allow us to test the validity of the Standard Model at the 10−4 level, and to explore new physics at a scale Λ > 10 TeV.
the reach on the contact couplings is better than the reach of the LEP II and SLC measurements by about an order of magnitude.
the polarized cross section measurement of e+e-→ e+e- process can provide a more stringent constraint on the left-handed contact interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sensitivity to contact couplings in e-e- collisions is comparable to the one in e+e- collisions.

, in the absence of new physics signals at the LHC, a Linear Collider with polarized beams would allow for the determination of the electron-lepton contact coupling constants to unprecedented precision, and hence for the discovery of the new physics responsible for them.
, for the same integrated luminosity, a Linear Collider with polarized beams is much more sensitive to contact-interactions than a Linear Collider without polarization.
